records.evidenceSource: Notion pricing page (Free tier with unlimited pages/blocks for individuals; Plus, Business, Enterprise paid tiers).
records.assignmentRationale: A robust free tier drives adoption; monetization occurs when individuals or teams convert to paid plans. The pricing structure is explicitly freemium.

records.evidenceSource: Notion web and mobile apps; no local installation; cloud-hosted workspaces.
records.assignmentRationale: The product is delivered entirely as a cloud application with shared infrastructure across workspaces—classic multi-tenant SaaS.

records.evidenceSource: Notion Business and Enterprise plan positioning; team billing and workspace administration features; conversion patterns in team contexts.
records.assignmentRationale: Despite a large individual user base, monetization and growth strategy prioritize teams and organizations. Paid conversion predominantly occurs in corporate and team contexts.
records.secondaryNotes: B2C is equally defensible given the volume of individual users; this profile emphasizes monetization strategy over user-count composition.

records.evidenceSource: Notion collaboration features (shared pages, team wikis, collaborative databases).
records.assignmentRationale: Platform value increases as more members of the same team adopt—shared workspaces and collaborative content become more useful with in-team participation.

records.evidenceSource: Notion adoption patterns documented in product marketing and community case studies (bottom-up team expansion).
records.assignmentRationale: Growth follows classic PLG: an individual adopts, invites teammates, the team converts to a paid plan, and usage scales within the organization without initial sales-led motion.

records.evidenceSource: Notion customer stories and implementation guides on replacing multiple tools (Confluence, Trello, Google Docs, wikis).
records.assignmentRationale: Adoption is hybrid in practice—Notion simultaneously substitutes several incumbent tools. Implementation challenges center on consolidating multiple systems into one workspace.
